## Reading a file {.smaller}

```python
with open("data/sequences.fasta") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line)
```

. . .

- `with` closes the file for you automatically 🚪
- The loop gives you **one line at a time** — works for huge files too

```python
line = line.strip()   # removes the invisible newline ⚠️
```

::: notes
`strip()` is essential — without it every comparison silently fails.
:::

## Parsing FASTA 🧬

```python
with open("data/sequences.fasta") as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith(">"):
            print("HEADER:", line)
        else:
            print("SEQUENCE of length", len(line))
```

. . .

This is the same logic as `grep ">"` — but now you can **compute** with it.

## Building a dictionary from a file {.smaller}

```python
sequences = {}
name = None

with open("data/sequences.fasta") as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith(">"):
            name = line[1:]          # drop the '>'
            sequences[name] = ""
        else:
            sequences[name] += line  # sequences can span many lines!

print(len(sequences), "sequences loaded")
```

::: notes
Walk through it line by line. This is the most complex code so far — take your time.
:::

## Writing a file 💾

```python
with open("results/report.txt", "w") as out:
    out.write("name\tlength\tGC\n")
    for name, seq in sequences.items():
        out.write(f"{name}\t{len(seq)}\t{gc_content(seq):.2f}\n")
```

. . .

`"w"` overwrites · `"a"` appends · `\n` = new line · `\t` = tab

::: {.callout-warning}
`"w"` destroys the old file without asking. Same rule as `>` in bash.
:::
